item.title: تصمیم سونی برای کنار گذاشتن قرارداد خود با خالق افسانه ای Metal Gear Solid، هیدئو کوجیما، برای بازی آینده پلی استیشن Physint ظاهراً نتیجه نگرانی های بودجه و از دست دادن ضرب الاجل ها بود.
item.description:
عملکرد درآمدی Death Stranding و دنباله آن، عامل دیگری که قبلاً توسط تحلیلگران ذکر شد، نیز در تصمیم سونی نقش داشته است.در حالی که عنوان اول سودی را برای Kojima Productions به ارمغان آورد، Death Stranding 2 نتوانست این موفقیت را تقویت کند.
تحلیل Alinea Analytics قبلاً نشان می‌دهد که فروش Death Stranding 2 اکنون کاهش یافته است، چندین تخفیف قابل‌توجه در این بازی نتوانسته است سوزن را جابه‌جا کند، و درآمد بازی برای بازی بسیار کمتر از سایر عوامل است.
گزارش بلومبرگ ادامه دارد.یکی تصمیم سونی است که قبلاً گزارش شده بود برای توقف انتشار بسیاری از بازی‌های تک‌نفره خود بر روی رایانه شخصی – چیزی که می‌توانست مخاطبان بالقوه Physint را بیشتر کند.و دلیل دیگر ظاهراً این است که، در حالی که کوجیما و پلی استیشن از زمان PS1 از شراکت طولانی با هم لذت می‌بردند، بسیاری از روسای سونی که قبلاً با خالق Metal Gear کار می‌کردند، از آن زمان به این سمت حرکت کردند.
با کاهش کوجیما، گزارش با جزئیاتی در مورد اینکه چرا Xbox بلافاصله از PlayStation ایمن شد، به غیر از PR، به طور واضح به سمت امنیت ناجیم رفت، بسته می‌شود.ادعا می‌شود که رهبران جدید ایکس‌باکس تحت مدیریت آشا شارما، Physint را به عنوان یک سرمایه‌گذاری قوی می‌دانستند، با برنامه‌ای برای راه‌اندازی این بازی بر روی رایانه شخصی (جای تعجب نیست) و به عنوان همسویی با هدف اعلام‌شده Sharma برای گسترش دامنه Xbox فراتر از بازی‌ها به فیلم و تلویزیون.به عنوان بخشی از اعلامیه اصلی سونی و کوجیما، نوعی از دخالت استودیوی فیلم مورد کنایه قرار گرفت - اگرچه دقیقاً چه چیزی در حال برنامه ریزی است، ما هنوز منتظر شنیدن آن هستیم.
ریس الیوت، تحلیلگر Alinea Analytics دیروز گفت: "این برای پلی استیشن در میان گیمرهای اصلی عالی به نظر نمی رسد.""به خصوص در حال حاضر. با این حال، از منظر کاملاً مالی، می توانم موقعیت سونی را درک کنم. به هر حال در خلاء.
بعدی از کوجیما، OD خواهد بود، پروژه ای شبیه به PT که قبلاً به ایکس باکس عرضه می شود. هنوز هیچ صحبتی در مورد زمان عرضه آن وجود ندارد، چه برسد به Physint - هر چند که بازی بعدی Kojimagen به عنوان یک بازی اعتباری توصیف شده است.
تولیدات.
تام فیلیپس سردبیر اخبار IGN است.

item.title: پس از پیمایش "بازنشانی" ایکس باکس، تیم شفر، رئیس Double Fine یک بار دیگر مستقل است.IGN با توسعه دهنده در مورد اتفاقات بعدی مصاحبه کرد.
item.description:
It's only been a few months since developer Double Fine's split from Microsoft, but the team behind Psychonauts 2, Kiln, and Keeper is looking ahead. With another successful Kickstarter campaign under its belt, the newly independent studio's second (or should that be third?) life as an indie is off to an optimistic start. With the current Kickstarter focusing on the developer's latest Amenesia Fortnight — a developer-run game jam where new micro games are produced — it's allowing the developers to build up some much-needed runway as they plan for their next major project.
At PAX West 2026, we spoke with Double Fine studio head and president, Tim Schafer, about the developer's current path forward. Along with talking about his return to independence following the biggest restructure in Xbox history, Schafer reflected on Double Fine's years under Microsoft's banner, and explained how Game Pass can still potentially work as a subscription service. He also reaffirmed his commitment to making Brutal Legend 2 (provided someone can front the money for it).
IGN: It's been seven years since the Microsoft acquisition, and the game industry has gone through so much change. What's it been like to return to being an independent developer?
Tim Schafer: It's been exhilarating. Like, it's scary because we've got to make our own way in the world, but we did that for 19 years before Microsoft, so we have a lot of great ideas and a lot of experience pitching them. A lot of people know it's a tough time out there. A lot of people, and now especially a lot of the older developers, are gone. A lot of the old avenues we used for funding are gone, but there are a lot of new ones. So we're just putting ourselves out there, meeting a lot of new people, and talking about who wants to make games with us.
IGN: I think what's been great to see with Double Fine is that it has a core audience of players that are invested in seeing the studio thrive. I remember the original Kickstarter campaign for Broken Age was a big breakthrough for Double Fine.
Schafer: Yeah, I mean that sort of thing was quite like a big financial impact, but it was also an awakening of just how tight we are with the community, like how dependent we are on them, and how much they're willing to participate. You know what I mean? Because they participate financially, but also creatively. Like, they really want to make art as well. I feel like that's something special about our fans, and it's because our number one thing is creativity. So I think it breeds a fan who also likes creativity, and I think it, hopefully, helps our games inspire not just players, but people to like learning to draw or program, or, you know, people who want to know how to make a game.
IGN: Now that you are an independent developer again, and with all this attention on you, do you feel there's a certain responsibility placed on you all to make it as an indie studio?
Schafer: I don't see it as a responsibility. I mean, I don't expect anybody to look at us and know what to do, because our situation always feels really unique to Double Fine and me. Like we're an indie game studio, but we have a lot of employees, and we have healthcare, and we have a lot of stuff like that. There's not a lot of companies our size anymore, like AA-size studios, kind of. So, I wouldn't say do everything that we do. I hope no one's following our example because I don't know if it works for anyone but us.
IGN: The Kickstarter for the Amnesia Fortnight is an interesting way to start this comeback, it's all about this big push to produce some new ideas and bring to life.
Schafer: It's kind of like a celebration of what we can do now that was harder to do before. Even being at PAX, Microsoft usually likes to have one big booth. So having little booths all over is not what they're into. They're not even here at the show. So being independent, we can come to PAX, we can talk to the fans, we can set the prices of our games. We can do tiny games like Thank You Bus Driver, which is a new project for us, and we made a whole special label for them called Double Fine Action Labs, where we can release smaller ideas, do game jams, and do the kind of things we like to do. So it's a celebration of both what we can do and what we like to do, which is high-bandwidth interaction with the fans, doing silly creative things, and just having a lot of fun.
IGN: I would be remiss not to say that a lot of people took notice of the Kickstarter mentioning that Brutal Legend 2 can be made if you secure $100 million. I understand it was meant as a joke…
Schafer: I mean, it was a joke, but also, it's not a joke. Sure, I mean, if we got $100 million, we would do it for sure. I would happily put everything aside and make Brutal Legend 2, as long as I could talk Jack Black into it. Yeah, but if we got $100 million, that's great. Yeah, I could do a demo for $100 [laughs]. But it's not a joke — I would do it if we hit that goal. We're probably not going to hit that, though. But any rich guys out there, if you ever want to see Brutal Legend 2, come help us out.
IGN: Now that you're back as an independent developer, how do you feel about those seven years working under Microsoft? Would you say that it was a valuable experience in the end?
Schafer: I learned a lot from it, and it was a really great experience overall. They invested a lot in the company, and their mission was to support Game Pass and other projects. So for a while, we were very closely aligned, and it was great. It was a great partnership, and then their goals changed, and so we parted ways because of that.
But I feel like, in the meantime, we had a great little collection of studios within Xbox Game Studios, like Compulsion, Ninja Theory, Obsidian, and inXile. We got to meet all the studio heads and talk to them, and our programmers got to talk. Their programmers are artists, and everyone was exchanging ideas and technology, and it was really a great learning experience about how other companies are run. So, because you're independent, you're a little more like an island. So, being an island that was temporarily pushed, hitched up to a bunch of other islands was very much, "Oh, that's a cool game right there, we could go play that game."
IGN: Game Pass was such a big part of the Xbox brand's push for a larger games audience. Do you feel that Game Pass still has value and potential as a service?
Schafer: I really want Game Pass to work. I like the idea of subscription models for companies like us, who, you know, lower the barrier to entry for everyone. We want to make games that are weird and creative, that you might not understand at first. I think that's the kind of stuff we like to do. Do people see the key art and go like, "What?" And if it's on a subscription, you've already kind of paid for the game. You'd be more likely to try it, so that sounds good.
But there are other ways to reach people like that, like lowering your prices, for example. You know, getting people to try your games like that. I think it could have worked. I don't understand why Netflix worked and Game Pass didn't, and I think that's something I just don't know enough about, but that's the way it is. So now we're taking another approach: making it really affordable.
IGN: It's been interesting to see the rise of these micro-games, ones that are fairly modest in concept, but offer variety and fun for groups of players. I know the term "friendslop" is used a lot, but I kind of see some of Double Fine's games, and experimental ones, being right at home with those styles of games – particularly Kiln.
Schafer: Yeah, I think the difference is multiplayer. We have built a ton of multiplayer, but the thing about those games kind of aligns with what we're doing with our Amnesia Fortnight, which is just trying stuff. A lot of those games came from game jams. I think the game Peak came from a game jam, and we just want to give everyone in the company a chance. Really, people feel safe to experiment and try creative ideas, and then to not spend $300 million on them, just spend like sticky bus drivers for six weeks, put it out there, and just see what you know.
The thing about those 'friendslop' games, people mostly focus on successes, but there's tons of them that don't work out. I think the idea is that you never know which one's going to take off, so don't bank the future of your company on any one individual idea for sure. But these games were called "friendjank" for awhile, you remember that? It's also about casual pacing, it's basically games where it's mostly about hanging out with your friends.
IGN: What are your thoughts on the state of the industry now? There's been a lot of reports and stories of developers struggling to stay open and some creatives having to leave the field. Do you feel optimistic that things can improve?
Schafer: It's a shitty time out there, and it's been getting worse for longer than I've ever seen it get worse. I usually try to comfort people by saying to the team, "Well, there are cycles, there are downturns, but it always turns back up again because you need people to make games, and that comes and goes." But this has been going on for at least four years, and I feel like I've never seen a cycle plunge so low.
Is it a permanent change in just the economics of it all? But people are still needed to make games. It's not like AI has replaced everybody, and for all the talk about it replacing Google, it's not effectively replacing anybody right now. So where are all those jobs going? I still see a bunch of games getting made, and people are still needed. So I wish I were smarter and knew the answer to that. But it seems like you need people to make games, and so there should be a ton of opportunities, and they're still making a lot of money.
For creatives, you have to have fun making games because they're really hard to make. A lot of these people could make more than money in a tech company, so they're here because they love games. And if you're here because you love games, then you should love what you're doing, love making games, and have fun.

item.title: نینتندو با هدف جلوگیری از فروش دستگاه هایی که دزدی دریایی بازی سوییچ را فعال می کنند، یک پیروزی حقوقی بزرگ به دست آورده است.
item.description:
البته این اولین باری است که نینتندو اقدام قانونی برای توقف فروش دستگاه‌های فعال کننده دزدی دریایی را آغاز می‌کند. سال گذشته، یک موددر کنسول نینتندو که از تعطیل کردن کسب‌وکار خود امتناع کرد - و سپس سعی کرد بدون وکیل از خود دفاع کند - توسط نینتندو به پرداخت 2 میلیون دلار دستور داده شد.مدتی را در زندان گذراند و به پرداخت 14.5 میلیون دلار غرامت محکوم شد، بدهی که او اکنون تا پایان عمر بازپرداخت خواهد کرد.
تام فیلیپس سردبیر اخبار IGN است.

item.title: پرتاب Toxic Commando جان کارپنتر کمتر از انتظارات ناشر Focus Entertainment بود، اما برای Saber Interactive از نظر تجاری موفقیت آمیز بود – و به گفته مدیر توسعه تیم Willits، کار فنی انجام شده برای آن به نفع Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 3 آینده خواهد بود.
item.description:
John Carpenter's Toxic Commando’s launch came in below publisher Focus Entertainment’s expectations, but for Saber Interactive it was successful in commercial terms — and according to development chief Tim Willits, the tech work done for it will go on to benefit the upcoming Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 3.
Toxic Commando builds upon Saber’s proprietary tech to present a zombie swarm for co-op players to gun down. It’s technology used for Saber’s World War Z, for the Tyranids in Space Marine 2, and will once again be utilized for the upcoming Space Marine 3.
In its recent financial report, Focus owner Pullup issued a somewhat downbeat note on Toxic Commander, which came out in March. But in an interview with IGN at gamescom, Saber’s Tim Willits was more positive, confirming it was a profitable project for the company.
“We're really happy with it,” he began. “Focus' opinion, they're a publicly traded company, so they have to say what they have to say. We'll leave that to them. But for us, we're really excited about it. We have some new stuff coming out. We actually have a good playerbase.
“It brought more people into the Saber universe. When I say Saber universe, it's people that fall in love with one game who now start to look at us, like Space Marine 2 with our 14 million players. It's f***ing ridiculous. Just a few! And then World War Z, remember that's 30 million people that played that game. It's nuts. More people played that game than saw the movie or read the book.”
Willits went on to say that the tech improvements made for Toxic Commander will be further improved for Space Marine 3. Indeed, you can trace a line from World War Z through Space Marine 2 and Toxic Commando right to Space Marine 3.
“[Toxic] was a well-made game that was fun to play, and it shows people what we do really well,” Willits said. “It shows people that Saber games are enjoyable to experience with your friends. It's over-the-top. It built on our technology. You'll see more of that in Space Marine 3. You can see the progression with our technology moves. I feel that it was a good brick in that Saber wall.
“We're growing the company, we're growing the project, we're growing the technology. It was profitable for us. We don't lose money. We don't lose money on anything.”
I asked Willits how Toxic Commando’s tech will be improved for Space Marine 3, and while he kept his cards close to his chest on actual game features, he did hint at an expanded scope.
“It's the maturity of the technology,” he said. “You can see the bigger swarms, you can see the bigger areas, you can see the better AI. There's cars — you didn’t have cars in Space Marine 2. I'm not saying we're going to have cars in Space Marine 3. I'm just saying the technology is growing and developing and that's our technology. So we can focus on technology pillars that will support our future games like Space Marine 3 and Jurassic Park — that uses the same technology.”
One of the big questions for Space Marine fans is how Saber will expand upon the gameplay. Space Marine 2 limits squads to three characters (modders increased this), and while some of the play spaces are big, there’s nothing you’d describe as having any sort of open world design. Willits has talked about three being the magic number for Space Marine 2 because of the maximum number of enemies it’s able to throw at squads — having four Space Marines, say, would make the game too easy and “scaling enemy assaults to justify bringing a fourth player was too great of a challenge.”
But could Space Marine 3 up the player count by upping the enemy count and playspace? Could it increase the scope of the battles, which in Space Marine 2 are limited in terms of area and units? Willits says he’s not saying Space Marine 3 will have cars, but it does beg the question: will Space Marine 3 have vehicles? A Land Raider, perhaps? Maybe some flying missions in a Gunship?
As for Saber's swarm tech, I'm not sure repeating the trick with Tyranids will be enough for Space Marine 3 after fans spent so much time with them in Space Marine 2. Most believe Space Marine 3 will feature the Necrons, based on hints sprinkled throughout Space Marine 2. But what other factions would fit the bill? A return to the Orks seen in Space Marine 1? (Orks are the primary antagonist of the 11th edition of the Warhammer 40,000 tabletop game.) How about a focus on the relentless Death Guard and swarms of shuffling Plaguebearers? Saber has form when it comes to zombies after all.
As for how Space Marine 3 development is going, Willits was very enthusiastic, but again didn’t give much away. Speaking of how well Space Marine 2 had gone (he previously told IGN its success had changed everything for Saber), Willits said the development team was now working to top it.
“The Emperor loves us. We are The Emperor’s favorite,” Willits joked. “All I can say is 3's going great. 2's been really successful. Our DLC's been super successful. People love the mods. It helps the team with experience, knowing what fans actually want, making sure that we adhere to the true Warhammer 40K universe franchise.
“The success of Space Marine 2 has really made the team passionate about making sure that Space Marine 3 is even better. They feel that there's this confidence and passion and vigor, and you can see it. When you talk to the team, they're just in it. So I'm really excited about that.”
Willits recently told IGN that no generative AI was being used in the development of Space Marine 3, after a backlash online to its use in Saber’s Rideshare Stimulator. Space Marine 3 currently does not have a release window.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: طبق گزارشی جدید، دنباله‌ی اجتناب‌ناپذیر Spider-Man: Brand New Day در حال حاضر کارگردان خود را دارد.
item.description:
ددلاین اعلام کرده است که دستین دانیل کرتون برای پنجمین فیلم مرد عنکبوتی با بازی تام هالند از مارول و سونی بازخواهد گشت.2.5 میلیون دلار بلیت فروخت و سومین فیلم پرفروش تاریخ شد.این همچنین بهترین باکس آفیس یک فیلم مرد عنکبوتی تا کنون و بزرگترین فیلم سال 2026 است — حداقل تا زمانی که Avengers: Doomsday فرود بیاید.
با گفتن همه اینها، کرتون در حال حاضر چیزهای زیادی در سر دارد، به این معنی که در دسترس بودن او مطمئن نبوده است.طرفداران مارول سال‌ها از او التماس می‌کردند که دنباله‌ای از شانگ چی بسازد، کاری که او قبلاً به طور مثبت در مورد اینکه هنوز می‌خواهد آن را انجام دهد، صحبت کرده بود.
اما اگرچه ممکن است Shang-Chi 2 اتفاق بیفتد یا نشود، Spider-Man 5 یک شرط مطمئن به نظر می‌رسد.تنها مشکل کرتون، در دسترس بودن خودش است، در میان مجموعه‌ای از پروژه‌های دیگر که او قبلاً آماده کرده است، از جمله فیلم Hawaii Five-O و اقتباس لایو اکشن ناروتو.با این حال، متأسفانه، پس از لغو ناگهانی سریال توسط دیزنی، کرتون دیگر روی فصل دوم مرد شگفت‌انگیز کار نخواهد کرد.
مرد عنکبوتی 5 چه زمانی می‌رسد؟اولین شکاف‌ها در برنامه اکران مارول در حال حاضر تا سال 2029 نیست، زمانی که این استودیو سه فیلم بدون عنوان برای عرضه دارد.(2027 فقط Avengers: Secret Wars را نمایش می‌دهد، در حالی که سال 2028 مملو از X-Men، Ghost Rider، و Black Panther 3 است.) با این حال، Spider-Man: Brand New Day در تابستان گذشته فیلمبرداری شد و کمتر از 12 ماه پس از آن منتشر شد، بنابراین به نظر می‌رسد کرتون بتواند یک بار دیگر برای پروژه‌های آینده خود بازگردد.
-M.ستاره فرنچایز، تام هالند، به طور خصوصی درباره بازگشت برای چندین حضور دیگر صحبت کرده است، اگرچه همچنین گفته است که اکنون به این فکر می کند که چگونه نقش را به یک قهرمان عنکبوتی جدید واگذار کند.شاید Spider-Man 5 زمانی باشد که ما در نهایت شاهد معرفی مایلز مورالز لایو اکشن با انیمیشن سه گانه Spider-Verse از سونی باشیم که همان شخصیت را در زمان ورود به نمایش می گذارد.زمان نشان خواهد داد، هرچند به نظر می رسد که کرتون در نهایت زمانی که دوربین ها رونمایی شوند، آنجا خواهد بود.

item.title: مگی رابرتسون گفته است که هر فرصتی را از کپکام برای ایفای مجدد نقش اصلی خود در نقش لیدی دیمیترسکو در مجموعه رزیدنت اویل می پذیرد و این شخصیت را "نخست زاده" خود می نامد.
item.description:
Maggie Robertson has said she would accept any opportunity from Capcom to reprise her breakout role as Lady Dimitrescu in the Resident Evil series, calling the character her “firstborn.”
Lady Dimitrescu, the towering face of Capcom’s phenomenally successful 2021 game, Resident Evil Village, was Robertson’s first video game role, and it changed her life forever.
Speaking to IGN at gamescom while promoting her latest video game gig — the sultry and scheming Tasha in upcoming Dungeons & Dragons game Warlock — Robertson said the last five years had been a surreal experience.
“That game, that character changed my life in every way,” she said. “There's no aspect of my life that has not been touched by that character. That was the very first game I ever did. And I had just done my graduate degree. I just came from a drama program. I lived the Hollywood dream in a surreal way. So I just graduated, moved to LA January 2019 and was throwing paint at the wall. I didn't have an agent. I was just self-submitting for things, seeing what stuck. I moved out here to pursue on-camera predominantly, but then this breakdown happened across my path and it was a day where I was just feeling like I might as well try something new. F**k it. Let's go for it. And it turned out to be this.”
Robertson said she had no idea which game or character she was auditioning for when she went in for Lady Dimitrescu, due to the secrecy that surrounds the video game industry, and even afterwards, could never have predicted the impact it would have.
“Video games also are always under NDA. So everything about the breakdown, the character names, the sides that I auditioned with, all of that was fake,” she said. “I had no idea what I was even auditioning for. I had no idea of the scope of what video games could offer me in terms of a career, in terms of acting, in terms of the roles that I would have access to.”
Such was the online popularity of Lady Dimitrescu following the character’s reveal ahead of Resident Evil Village’s release, that Capcom thrust her into the forefront of the game’s marketing. Lady Dimitrescu appeared on billboard advertising, in viral social media posts, and was in pretty much every Resident Evil Village trailer as Capcom doubled down on the vociferous fandom that emerged around the character.
Fast forward five years, and Robertson has acted in everything from Baldur’s Gate 3 (Orin the Red), to Fortnite (DJ PJ). In Warlock, Robertson plays another Dungeons & Dragons villain, Tasha, patron to the playable character. Such is Robertson’s fame within the video game industry that she appeared on-stage at Opening Night Live last month to introduce Warlock gameplay. And there are more video game roles to come.
“Ultimately, I'm so grateful for it because I think my type with theater, my type with on-camera, the roles that I am so right for are roles that are waiting for me when I am 50 and 60 years old,” she continued. “And I didn't have access to those at the time that I was entering the industry. And being able to become a part of this industry helped me have access to those roles now. And I didn't have to wait. I didn't have to be limited by the way that I looked. Again, it's like, if you imagine yourself, if you can imagine it, you can be it. And I find that so liberating.
“But that is the Hollywood dream. That is what they sell you, is that you never know when your big break is going to happen. You never know what opportunity is going to be your next big break. And that happened to me. I just said yes on a random thing.”
The big question for Resident Evil fans is whether Lady Dimitrescu might appear in another game in the series, or perhaps in an animation or maybe even in live-action. Capcom has yet to say either way, but Robertson would jump at the chance.
“Oh, of course!” she said. “A hundred times, yes. She's my firstborn. So anytime they call, I will say happy days.”
For now, though, the focus is on Warlock and her character, Tasha. "What I like most about Tasha is that she's neither good nor evil," Robertson said. "She's complex in that way. She can go either way depending on the day. I think that gives you a lot of fun to play with. She's so charming and charismatic, but also cunning, and is ultimately looking after number one, which is herself. And she'll help you for sure, but there's always something in it for her if she decides to help you. And you don't always know what that is. So I found her to be a nicely complex character. I always like getting to work on those."

بر کسی پوشیده نیست که بازی های دستی در حال حاضر کمی در دوران رنسانس است.توسط Nintendo Switch راه اندازی شد و توسط Steam Deck به جلو منتقل شد.در کنار این عرضه های اصلی، دسته دیگری از گوشی های دستی هستند که بیشتر به گذشته نسبت به آینده هدف گذاری شده اند.به ویژه، گوشی‌های دستی دو صفحه‌نمایش مجهز به اندروید مانند Retroid Pocket Duo جدید، سخت‌افزار طراحی‌شده برای شبیه‌سازی Nintendo DS و 3DS را ارائه می‌کنند.
item.description:
همین الانبا استفاده از Nintendo Switch و توسط Steam Deck و رایانه‌های شخصی قدرتمندتر دستی مانند MSI Claw 8 EX AI+، هیچ‌وقت گزینه‌های بیشتری برای انجام بازی‌ها بر روی صفحه‌نمایش کوچک وجود ندارد، چه خارج از خانه باشد یا فقط در اطراف خانه بدون اتصال به کنسول.
در کنار این نسخه‌های معمولی، کلاس دیگری از بازی‌های دستی مورد استفاده در آینده بیشتر است.به طور خاص، گوشی‌های دستی دو صفحه‌نمایش مجهز به اندروید مانند AYN Thor، سخت‌افزار طراحی‌شده برای شبیه‌سازی Nintendo DS و 3DS را ارائه می‌کنند.این هفته، Retroid وارد رقابت‌های جدید Pocket Duo خود شد و امروز ما اکنون می‌دانیم که قیمت آن چقدر است.
Retroid Pocket Duo برای مدل پرچم‌دار که با 8 گیگابایت رم و 128 گیگابایت فضای ذخیره‌سازی عرضه می‌شود، 270 دلار قیمت خواهد داشت، اگرچه کوپنی برای کاهش قیمت 20 دلاری وجود دارد.همچنین یک مدل ارزان‌تر Pocket Duo Lite با نصف رم و فضای ذخیره‌سازی وجود دارد که قیمت آن 150 دلار خواهد بود.هر دو مدل در رنگ‌های مختلفی عرضه می‌شوند، از جمله رنگ‌هایی که یادآور رنگ بنفش GameCube، سفید مایل به خاکستری Game Boy، و آبی شفاف و بنفش اتمی هستند.پیش‌سفارش‌ها در حال حاضر تمام شده‌اند.
Pocket Duo یک صفحه‌نمایش اصلی 5.5 اینچی 1080p AMOLED ارائه می‌کند، در حالی که صفحه‌نمایش دوم 4.5 اینچی با وضوح 960p است.این پردازنده از پردازنده Qualcomm Dragonwing Q-7790 پشتیبانی می‌کند و اندروید 16 را اجرا می‌کند که بازی‌های زیادی را از طریق فروشگاه Play ارائه می‌کند، همچنین گزینه‌های متعددی را برای DS، 3DS و دیگر شبیه‌سازی‌های سیستم قدیمی ارائه می‌دهد.اگر به این مسیر بروید، بازی‌ها را باید به صورت قانونی به دست آورید، مثلاً با ریختن کارتریج‌های بازی خود - IGN تحت هیچ شرایطی از دزدی دریایی چشم پوشی نمی‌کند.
هنوز اطلاعاتی در مورد زمان عرضه‌ی Pocket Duo و Duo Lite وجود ندارد، اما این قیمت‌ها آن را به جایگزینی عالی برای AYN Thor تبدیل می‌کند که یک اسنپ‌دراگون با قدرت کمتر یا Snapdragon 295 یا 58 دلاری ارائه می‌کند.مدل «پایه» با قیمت 329 دلار به نسخه قدرتمندتر اسنپدراگون 8 نسل 2 می رسد.پیش‌سفارش‌ها در حال حاضر تمام شده‌اند، اما این گوشی‌های دستی معمولاً به صورت موجی در دسترس هستند، بنابراین اگر مایل به خرید هستید، مراقب قیمت‌های بعدی باشید.در عین حال، ما به دنبال استفاده از Pocket Duo هستیم، بنابراین با نزدیک‌تر شدن به عرضه، منتظر بررسی ما باشید.
Bo Moore مدیر ارشد فناوری IGN است.می توانید او را به صورت آنلاین @usebomswisely پیدا کنید.

همانطور که Entertainment Weekly اشاره می کند، نقاط Optimus Prime در DHS نیز به دلیل آمدن در پاشنه مرگ پیتر کالن، بازیگری که ده ها سال صداپیشگی Optimus را بر عهده داشت، مورد انتقاد قرار گرفت.
آخرین بازی کالن به عنوان رهبر نمادین Autobot در Optimus Prime: The Awakening با اکران های کوتاه سالگرد 4 نمایش داده می شود.فیلم.
دولت ترامپ به طور گسترده از تصاویر (اغلب با هوش مصنوعی) و ویدیوهایی که فرهنگ پاپ را مناسب می‌کنند در پست‌های رسانه‌های اجتماعی خود استفاده می‌کند.
پست‌های Optimus Prime از DHS پس از ویدیوی هوش مصنوعی کاخ سفید که پرزیدنت ترامپ را به‌عنوان فانوس سبز نشان می‌دهد و انتشار طرح‌های جدید نیروی فضایی با لباس‌هایی شبیه به یونیفورم‌های جنگی Empire منتشر می‌شود.فرنچایز یا توسط سربازان در Starship Troopers، یک فیلم علمی تخیلی که فاشیسم را تحقیر می کند.

ساندرسون و مجری همکارش، دن ولز، پادکست این هفته را با بحث در مورد چند کارت جدید که در نوامبر امسال منتشر می شوند، آغاز کردند.به طور خاص، ساندرسون به کارت قرمز تک رنگ کاپیتان جیمز تی کرک اشاره کرد که نشان می داد آنچه آنها توافق کردند "یک کرک کامل" بود.
ساندرسون در مورد کارت گفت: "من فکر می کردم کرک آنها واقعا باهوش بود.""اگر هیچ گزینه ای ندارید، او آنها را به شما می دهد، درست است؟ او یک کارت برای شما می کشد و/یا شما یک کارت را دور می اندازید و سپس یکی را می کشید. بنابراین اگر کارتی در دست ندارید، به شما یک کارت می دهد. بنابراین او مشکلات حل نشدنی را حل می کند، او یک پیراهن قرمز می سازد و تیم شما را با یک سخنرانی هیجان انگیز تشویق می کند."تی کرک از سری اصلی.این کارتی است که می‌توانید از مجموعه پایه بیرون بکشید، برخلاف یکی از Commander Decks برای پیش‌سفارش.مجموعه‌های MTG Star Trek تا اواخر نوامبر منتشر نمی‌شوند، بنابراین مشخص نیست که این کارت در حال حاضر چقدر رایج است.
در مورد اینکه چرا براندون ساندرسون در پادکست خود در این هفته در مورد آن صحبت می‌کند، ما فقط می‌توانیم حدس بزنیم.ممکن است او فقط عاشق Star Trek و Magic the Gathering باشد و بخواهد مدتی را صرف صحبت کردن در مورد آن کند.با این حال، تمایل او به اقتباس‌های رومیزی و علاقه آشکار به Magic the Gathering چیز دیگری را نشان می‌دهد.این شاید فقط نشانه دیگری باشد که نشان می دهد همکاری Universes Beyond برای کتاب های گسترده Cosmere ساندرسون در دست ساخت است.
این دقیقاً یک نظریه جدید نیست، زیرا طرفداران متقاعد شده اند که همکاری ساندرسون در MTG برای مدتی اجتناب ناپذیر است.خارج از علاقه شخصی خود، ساندرسون رابطه مداوم خود را با Wizards of the Coast هنگامی که در مارس 2025 به طور انحصاری کارت جدیدی را برای Tarkir Dragonstorm پیش‌نمایش کرد، به نمایش گذاشت. همچنین در Reddit بحث‌هایی در مورد چگونگی ایجاد مجموعه سفارشی Stormlight Archive وجود دارد.
با این بازی جدید و انبوه تلویزیون اپل، Stormttar بعداً در راه است.سال، من مطمئناً کراس اوور MTG مانند این را در آینده رد نمی کنم.
Jacob Kienlen یک استراتژیست ارشد توسعه مخاطب و نویسنده برای IGN است.او که در پورتلند، اورگان به دنیا آمده و بزرگ شده است، شمال غربی را خانه خود برای تمام زندگی خود می داند.با مدرک لیسانس در ارتباطات و 10 سال تجربه نویسندگی حرفه ای، تخصص او در موضوعات مختلف فرهنگ پاپ - از سریال های تلویزیونی گرفته تا کتاب ها و جدیدترین مجموعه های لگو - پخش شده است.

item.title: GameStop در حال برنامه ریزی برای بازگشایی فروشگاه هایی است که قبلاً تعطیل کرده بود و یکی از آنها این هفته درهای خود را باز می کند.
item.description:
بازی را قبلاً متوقف کنیداین هفته درهای خود را باز کرد.
شرکت این برنامه‌ها را از طریق رسانه‌های اجتماعی خود اعلام کرد و فاش کرد که این عرضه در 11 سپتامبر آغاز خواهد شد. IGN با GameStop تماس گرفت تا ببیند چند فروشگاه در حال بازگشایی هستند و بیانیه زیر از سوی سخنگوی GameStop به او داده شد:
"تعداد این است: حداقل یک نفر، از فردا. همانطور که برای مابقی، Gametopel بسته است."
اکنون فروشگاه‌ها از 11 سپتامبر در سراسر کشور بازگشایی می‌شوند. pic.twitter.com/OKbS0WAmy4
اعلام چنین اعلامیه‌ای بر اساس تنها یک فروشگاه کمی سرگرم‌کننده است، اما برای کسانی که می‌خواهند مکان این فروشگاه خاص را بدانند، می‌توانند آن را در اوهایو در آدرس زیر پیدا کنند:در مورد اینکه چند فروشگاه دیگر قصد دارند دوباره احیا شوند صحبت کنیم، اما امیدواریم که به زودی اخبار بیشتری منتشر شود.
GameStop در نیم دهه گذشته تا حدودی به لطف ظهور بازی های دیجیتال، سهم نسبتاً زیادی از مشکلات داشته است.این شرکت از سال 2020 بیش از هزار فروشگاه را بسته است و در طول سال ها هزینه ها را به روش های دیگر کاهش داده است.GameStop همچنین برای مدت کوتاهی Game Informer، یک مجله بازی را که متعلق به خرده‌فروش بود و در فروشگاه‌های آنها فروخته می‌شد، نابود کرد.Game Informer به ناچار صاحب جدیدی پیدا کرد، اما نزدیک به یک سال طول کشید تا مجله را بازگرداند.
اکنون، GameStop یک مانع دیگر برای غلبه بر آن دارد: مرگ قریب الوقوع بازی های فیزیکی.پلی استیشن اعلام کرد که پشتیبانی از بازی های فیزیکی را در سال 2028 پایان می دهد، که به نظر می رسد نشان می دهد PS6 از هیچ نوع دیسک پشتیبانی نمی کند.هیئت منصفه هنوز درباره برنامه ایکس باکس با کنسول بعدی خود صحبت نمی کند، اما در هر صورت، رسانه های فیزیکی بازی در حال شروع به حذف تدریجی توسط صنعت هستند.GameStop ممکن است بتواند این طوفان را پشت سر بگذارد، زیرا مدتی است که کلکسیون‌ها و آیتم‌های عجیب‌تری مانند Funko Pops ارائه می‌دهد.GameStop همچنین در تلاش است تا eBay را خریداری کند، که به تنوع بخشیدن به شرکت کمک می کند.
عکس براندون بل/گتی ایماژ
کید اوندر یک مترجم آزاد برای تیم خبری IGN است.او همه چیزهای سرگرمی، از جمله بازی، فیلم و موارد دیگر را پوشش می دهد.می توانید او را در توییتر @Cade_Onder پیدا کنید.

item.title: راجر کلارک بازیگر Red Dead Redemption 2 فاش کرد که سرفه‌های شدید آرتور مورگان در واقع زمانی ضبط شده است که او در زندگی واقعی بیمار بوده است.
item.description:
این مقاله حاوی اسپویل‌هایی برای Red Dead Redemption 2 است.
بازیگر Red Dead Redemption 2 راجر کلارک فاش کرده است که سرفه‌های شدید آرتور مورگان در واقع زمانی ضبط شده است که او در زندگی واقعی بیمار بود.
من اخیراً با راجر کلارک برای یک ویدیوی YouTube در مورد نحوه برخورد آرتور مورگان از Red Deadcraft مصاحبه کردم.در طول گفتگوی طولانی‌مان، توانستم از او چیزی بپرسم که همیشه به آن فکر می‌کردم: تظاهر به سرفه‌های خشونت‌آمیز مانند آرتور چقدر دشوار است؟به گفته کلارک، در واقع آنقدرها هم بد نیست - و در برخی موارد، او حتی تظاهر هم نمی کرد.
کلارک گفت: «آنقدرها هم که فکر می کنید بد نیست، زیرا من پنج سال فرصت داشتم تا آن را منتشر کنم."اگر یک صحنه سرفه واقعا بد وجود داشت، ما همیشه آن را برای پایان روز ذخیره می‌کردیم. بنابراین، آنقدرها هم که فکر می‌کنید بد نبود. پنج سال فرصت داشتم تا آن را کنار بگذارم. در پنج سال، سرماخوردگی‌های زیادی وجود داشت. داده‌های زیادی به دست آوردیم که کاملاً واقعی بودند. [...] من مثل "هی، بگذار سرما بخورم."و آنها می‌گویند، "خوب."[...] خلط خوب است."
در واقع هیچ راهی بهتر از تجربه واقعی صحنه در زندگی واقعی خود برای عمل وجود ندارد.آرتور مورگان تقریباً تا حدی با سرفه‌هایش تعریف می‌شود.این شخصیت در اوایل داستان پس از کتک زدن مردی تا حد مرگ به خاطر مقداری پول به بیماری سل مبتلا می شود.این تقریباً یک مجازات بی‌رحمانه کارمایی برای زندگی است که آرتور انجام داده است و بسته به انتخاب بازیکن، آنها می‌توانند با کمک به دیگران سعی کنند کابوی را نجات دهند.
هر چه بازی ادامه می‌یابد، سرفه‌های آرتور بدتر و بدتر می‌شود.بازیکن در ابتدا نمی‌دانست که چرا آرتور اینقدر بیمار است، تا اینکه شروع به هک کردن ریه‌هایش می‌کند، از حال می‌رود و برای تشخیص درست به نزد پزشک کشیده می‌شود.این یک مسیر منحصر به فرد برای بازی در آن است، و بخشی از چیزی است که داستان Red Dead Redemption 2 را به یاد ماندنی می کند.
Cade Onder یک فریلنسر برای تیم خبری IGN است.او همه چیزهای سرگرمی، از جمله بازی، فیلم و موارد دیگر را پوشش می دهد.می توانید او را در توییتر @Cade_Onder پیدا کنید.

item.title: گیلرمو دل تورو، فیلمساز تحسین شده، در مورد افکار خود در مورد هوش مصنوعی و آنچه احساس می کند در فرآیند خلاقانه هنگام استفاده از هوش مصنوعی گم می شود صحبت کرد.
item.description:
Acclaimed filmmaker Guillermo Del Toro spoke out about his thoughts on artificial intelligence and what he feels gets lost in the creative process when AI is used in art.
Del Toro popped into the r/movies subreddit for an AMA session with fans on September 9. One of these fans, going by the username ihs25ysf, asked him about some comments he’d made during a 2024 talk at the British Film Institute, where he said that AI can create “semi-compelling screensavers” and “that’s essentially that.”
“The value of art is not in how much it costs and how little effort it requires," he said at the time. "It's how much would you risk to be in its presence."
Guillermo Del Toro on AI, emotion and the value of art.Watch the full In Conversation on our YouTube channel.@RealGDT pic.twitter.com/XxO05Fpea7
The Pan’s Labyrinth creator has been adamant that the human element of art be preserved — something for which he continued to advocate in his response to the fan, who asked him for his opinion on the “biggest thing lost” when a “computer generates an image instead of a human hand.”
To Del Toro, the “alchemy” of creativity and discovery humans experience when crafting a story or artwork is unachievable by a machine, and many of the best works are often elevated by "accidents" that happen during the creative process.
“The three quarters of the process that gave you the chance to think of the idea that people don't think about without that process,” he answered. “Meaning, AI can get you to the middle really fast, but there's a dialectic with the process that gets you to that top 10%.”
He went on to use the Pale Man from Pan’s Labyrinth as an example of this, describing how its design was inspired by an unlikely combination of a manta ray and artwork on a poster for Don Coscarelli’s Phantasm.
“We sculpted it as an old man, with a face," he continued. "And then I said, ‘Let's take out the face.’ This happened because I saw a photo of a manta ray and the poster for Don Coscarelli’s Phantasm. That combination, which happened at two different times during a week or a month, are not permutations that are chemically part of an equation. They are alchemy. And then I said, ‘Take out the face,’ and then I said,’ Let's put the eyes on the hands.’ This triangulation happens because I spent a month or two months living with the idea of this creature. And it's not linear.”
Del Toro brought up a conversation he had with Christopher Nolan about The Odyssey (which he previously shared with IGN), where he asked the director how he’d managed to convincingly pull off Odysseus and his crew braving Poseidon’s stormy seas.
“AI is like a super-fast engine that makes semi-sentient permutations of things that are already done," he said. "Creation is things that have never been done. Coming to exist. And the second thing is the loss of the apprenticeship that one has as an artist. You're never a master; you're always an apprentice. This is a kinship I have with, for example, Chris Nolan. When he showed me The Odyssey, there’s a scene when Matt Damon is floating in the stormy ocean and I asked him — because we were talking about practical effects, and how great it is and that we both always use a maquette or a model — and I asked him, ‘How did you do it?’ He said, ‘We put him in a storm in the ocean.’”
In another delightful anecdote, Del Toro mentioned a past conversation with James Cameron on the set of Terminator 2, describing how Cameron used “accidents” to increase audience immersion and overall believability.
“You're gonna find that 30% of a great image occurs accidentally. You know, either a drop of water hits the lens, or the camera shakes. I remember when in 1993, '94, Jim Cameron and I became friends very fast. And we were looking at Terminator 2. And he was showing me the scene where Robert Patrick is in the back of the car, and he breaks the window with his arm. And he said, ‘You see those flares?’ I said yeah. He said, ‘We put them there, because the audience thinks an image is real, if you put an accident in it.’ That's true. And I agree. The accident is vital. And the best accidents are things you don't court. They just occur from the interaction with reality,” he said.
We got the chance to speak with Guillermo Del Toro as part of our IGN30 Icons Series, where he revealed how much he loved The Odyssey’s cyclops and told us about his favorite video games — one of which might surprise you.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: تقلب در بازی‌های ویدیویی به یک صنعت چند میلیارد دلاری تبدیل شده است که فرنچایزهایی مانند Call of Duty را مجبور کرده است که تیم‌های کاملی را برای مبارزه با این همه‌گیری بسازند.
item.description:
Cheating in video games has turned into a multi-billon dollar industry, one that has forced franchises like Call of Duty to build entire teams to combat this epidemic. One of the people leading the charge is a man named David Andrews, a former Department of Defense contractor and member of the Air Force who made the leap into the video game industry. He began this career change working at Rockstar Games, helping combat cheating in Grand Theft Auto Online. Last year, he made the jump to Activision to become the Senior Director of Game Security for Call of Duty.
IGN had the opportunity to sit down with Andrews and peel back the layers on Call of Duty's anti-cheat system, Ricochet. Andrews disspelled myths about Call of Duty's anti-cheat, offered clarity on the process of how they investigate suspected cheaters, how they've hired cheater makers to combat the problem, and much more. It's a rare opportunity, as there's a lot of caution around publicly speaking about anti-cheat in gaming. If you say too much, you could inadvertedly give cheaters a heads-up on how to evade detective, after all.
With that said, we drilled down on Call of Duty's long running issue with cheaters in an attempt to make it less mysterious. It's an important subject ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release in October and something Activision is working hard to spotlight.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity and length.
IGN: Before we dive specifically into Call of Duty, tell me the difference between working on Grand Theft Auto Online, Red Dead Online, and Call of Duty, because one's obviously hyper-competitive, while Grand Theft Auto is a completely different ecosystem.
David Andrews: I think the interesting pivot for me is that the GTA Online gameplay loop is very different. Same thing for Red Dead Online, and that's where cheat developers tend to go. They're trying to shortcut whatever that gameplay loop is for their customers. And so on GTA and Red Dead, it was much more about economic progress within the world. So we had problems with money drop lobbies and things like that in the old bad days on GTA Online, which we did eventually fix. The nature of the cheating is different there. In terms of the impact and the disruption that it can cause to the players, very similar.
[There are] persistent online sessions in GTA Online versus rolling lobbies on Call of Duty. A cheater that goes undetected for too long is going to have an impact no matter what that is. There was also lots of griefing in GTA Online powered by cheats and things like that. As different as the core gameplay loops are between the two games, and you could probably say this about anything across the industry, cheating is still just ultimately super disruptive. It's a terrible experience. It's bad for our players, and the mission is always just to try to prevent as many of them as we can from getting into the game and then get them out as quickly as we can for those that make it through.
IGN: Is there something that companies can do together to solve these issues? I saw you last night talking about Wardogs and their approach. Everyone has a different strategy, but is there anything the industry can collectively do?
David Andrews: There's a ton of overlap that we see within the industry. It is an industry-wide problem. If anybody running a live service title is going to have this kind of issue with cheating, and no matter how advanced or what your particular approach is for a particular title or whatever you're doing, cheaters are always going to get through. I thought that a really good message from that Wardogs video was that no matter how good you are at this part of the game, people are going to get through. Cheat developers are incredibly financially incentivized. It's a multi-billion dollar industry out there selling cheats, and they're all looking for their cut of it. I think in terms of what we can do as a group, we definitely all talk with each other informally, always trading war stories and maybe some approaches in terms of what's going on.
Certainly I've seen in my past at Rockstar as well as here at Activision, you'll have cheat developers and cheat resellers out there that are selling not just for one title. There's very rarely somebody who's just developing for Call of Duty. They might have their fingers in Fortnite or Valorant or some other title out there, as well. There's usually opportunities for us to compare notes a little bit whenever that's possible for us to do. By and large though, we all keep pushing forward in terms of all of the things that are available to us. Different companies have different litigation strategies and things like that, but we're all marching in the same direction as much as we can.
IGN: What have you learned about cheatmakers? What’s the motive? It’s hard to wrap my head around why someone would pay $70 for a game just to not really play it.
David Andrews: Money is totally a huge motive for quite a lot of them, but there are also a strain of cheat developers, or I even call them cheat development-adjacent folks, who are just in it for the love of the game. They just really love that title and they have a technical sort of bent of mind and they want to understand how the game is working. And then that naturally leads into this place where you might be putting together a cheat to figure out ‘How does this game actually work?’
And in that space, I've had some success in turning some of those cheat developers or cheat-adjacent people to the light side by basically, bringing them over, and hiring them into the team. They bring a huge expertise and a really unique point of view to add to the team, and it can be a really huge value add for us. We've done that successfully a few times.
I think for their users, the motivation is like you mentioned: You pay $70 or whatever it is for a title just to not play it. It's because they want to be seen to be good and they're not actually good at this game. They kind of suck, which is fair enough. I'm not the best at Call of Duty myself personally, but I wouldn't turn to a cheat to go try to do something about that. But they are in friend groups, they're in social circles that really highly prize competency at these games. And so they go out and this is their only option to be any good at them, so they go out and buy cheats.
IGN: I’d love some insight into the cat-and-mouse game, since there’s a whack-a-mole situation that likely happens with trying to stomp out cheatmakers. There will always be cheaters, regardless of the steps you take.
David Andrews: The main mission is always just to protect the integrity of that live legitimate player experience, just making sure that they're having the best possible experience the way that our game developers intended for them to have. We do that a lot of different ways. The cat-and-mouse game is absolutely part of this, and there's some balancing efforts that go in there, in terms of figuring out when's the right time to ban a cheater once you've detected them. I think in the past, quite a lot of us in the industry indexed pretty heavily towards ban waves for a variety of reasons. One of them is that if you catch enough of the cheat customers in one big roundup, you might knock that cheat offline for a period of time and you actually get more clean running than you would otherwise by just issuing bans as you get them.
That's certainly where I started out philosophically, but as the years have gone on, I don't necessarily believe that that's the most effective way anymore. I think the most effective way is shifting left, preventing cheaters from getting into the game and then once they get into the game, getting them out as quickly as possible. Every single ban that we do gives feedback to the cheat developers and it helps them troubleshoot their problem, which is how did we detect them? It gives them feedback on how to circumvent us, but then that's just a challenge for us to get better at our jobs and do a better job of creating new detections, creating new novel ways of finding cheaters, preventing them and getting them out of the game.
There are a lot of conspiracies about cheating in Call of Duty, such as maybe the perception of how bad it really is due to viral clips. From your perspective, what are some of the myths of the cheating situation in Call of Duty?
David Andrews: I think you've touched on one there. The numbers that we see internally remain really, really positive. We shared during the Black Ops 7 beta that we had a very, very low match infection rate. That's maintained over the course of the title. It's incredibly low. If you're an average player and you're in ranked or you're in Warzone, you're doing whatever you want, you're not encountering a lot of cheaters. But [if] you go on social media and [watch] content creators and pros, they're having a different experience to what you're probably having, and then you're sort of internalizing that. You're seeing, ‘Well, my favorite streamer is encountering cheaters every day.’ I go online, I see something unfair or something inexplicable that I'm not quite sure what happened there. I'm just going to assume that's a cheater as well because I've seen this around. It just doesn't tend to be true for our average players.
Our match infection rate is incredibly good still, but that does still highlight for us that there are hotspots. There are problem areas. We don't want to try to go out there and say ‘We've solved cheating, you're never going to see a cheater.’ Certainly content creators and pro players that are playing at the very tip top edge of ranked play are going to encounter more cheaters right now. We're working on it all the time to try and get them out of the game.
That's the biggest one I think right now. Perception is just quite prevalent that there's a huge cheating problem. It's not to say there is no cheating problem. Obviously Ricochet still exists. We're all still gainfully employed and we're still trying to work on this problem, but it's certainly taken a pretty giant step forward with Black Ops seven with the introduction of TPM and Secure Boot requirements, and we're looking to just keep making more steps forward in the next title.
I wanted to ask a little bit about the review process. So, say I'm suspected of cheating. I've been reported and you guys are going to take a look at my account. What does that look like? Is there a human reviewing it? Is it AI-reviewed? And how long do they spend looking at that? Because I imagine there are a lot of reports. So, how do you sift through that to make sure you guys are giving its due diligence?
David Andrews: I'll say that things come in from a variety of different directions, and the vast majority of our bans that go out are through reviewed but automated systems. So for instance, for a particular cheat, we might deploy a signature that identifies like, ‘Oh, in running memory, if you see this string, this string only exists for this cheat.’ And then we fire that back and we'll collect that data for a little bit on all those accounts that are triggering that detection, look at them en masse, and also one by one and just make sure that those really do look like cheaters. That process is pretty involved.
We look at game data, we have everything that you input into the game clients while you're in a match. All of that data is with us and so we can identify clear outliers there. We also look at trends and behavior, like what is your kill death ratio over time? Does it spike in certain circumstances? What's your win-loss ratio? Things like that. We also will look at replay renders. We have tooling internally that we can just recreate an entire match and look at it and see if it looks suspicious or not. These are just some of the tools that we have internally. So we'll apply that to that whole batch, that whole population of potentially detected cheaters. And if it passes through that validation stage, then we'll say, ‘Okay, that signature is good. People that are popping that signature are going to get banned from now on.’ There's also things that are more manual. All the same tools kind of apply.
We'll still look at the account holistically. We'll look at it per match. We'll look at it in terms of how often they are being reported. All these kinds of data points are valuable to us and then we'll make a determination. That's kind of the stuff that you might see if a social media clip is posted and they aren't already banned. These are the things that we start looking into to see, ‘Okay, well what's going on with this account? What do their last few matches look like? Let's try to make a determination here.’
IGN: There was an incident a week or two ago with a former COD pro player named FormaL, and he triggered the detection in the Modern Warfare 4 beta. Call of Duty’s social team said that wasn’t supposed to happen. Do you know what happened there? What is the percentage of people being banned that shouldn't be banned, and what's the process of making sure that doesn't happen?
Former Call of Duty pro and legend FormaL got permanently banned in the Modern Warfare 4 beta live on stream 💀The Oris is so good it’s got pros getting their accounts flagged 🤣 pic.twitter.com/8MlHBfbH3G
David Andrews: So, the thing I'll say for that one is I think, obviously, we replied to that particular instance, but he certainly wasn't the only person that was caught up in that slight error there. Betas are for us, as well. We're constantly kind of tuning and testing our systems and transitioning from Black Ops 7 to Modern Warfare 4. There's a lot of tuning that has to take place there to make sure that all of our behavioral thresholds are accurate.
Also, someone like that player is quite high, and so very highly skilled players are kind of constantly brushing up against the threshold where we say ‘Beyond this, no human could achieve that.’ So they're just right there. They're quite close. And so we constantly are looking at this. The answer to the question is really, we're constantly reviewing the output of our systems. We don't just do that review one time and then we set it and forget it.
We're constantly looking back to see, ‘Is this thing still performant?’ Because also we want to know that we're still catching cheaters, but also is it overperforming? Is it catching people that it shouldn't be catching? We've built quite a lot of safeguards over the years. One of the things that impressed me coming in [is that] if there's some conjunction of events where a false enforcement is issued, we tend to catch it fairly quickly and then we will kind of identify systematically who were all the people impacted.
So in that one, it was one of about 200 people, I think, that were caught over the course of both beta weekends with that particular problem. We identified the problem, which won't happen again, and we restored all those people to good standing. So it's just constant review, constant monitoring, always looking at what's going on.
Do you have any involvement with the videos of process servers showing up to people’s houses to give them a cease and desist, or are you just enjoying them?
David Andrews: I certainly enjoy it for sure. I think that we do have a pretty comprehensive grasp on everything that's going on within the cheat community, and that extends to trying to identify devs and potentially put together actions like that. We don't necessarily initiate litigation or send cease and desists to everybody. There is some prioritization and triaging that has to happen. We do go after popular cheats obviously, but we also go after cheats that are technologically sort of more advanced than other cheats as well. And for these incredibly persistent cheat developers who are, again, just enormously financially incentivized, it kind of doesn't matter how often we detect them sometimes. And they'll gaslight their own customers into thinking like, 'Oh, it was you. It was your behavior and game that got you banned. It's not my cheat that got you banned.' And so when they're that stuck in, they're that persistent, they're that sticky, we have to do things like that and certainly the team helps contribute to that.
IGN: I would love to know your stance on how you guys are supporting older Call of Duty games, as cheaters are out there taking advantage of the fact that nobody's really watching them because they're older games.
David Andrews: Yeah, that's unfortunately one that I won't be able to answer.
Editor’s note: Activision linked IGN to a statement recently provided to Windows Central regarding an update that patched out a security issue with the original Modern Warfare 2. The statement notes that more support updates for older Call of Duty games are coming soon: "An update released this week addressed all known vulnerabilities in Modern Warfare 2. The team continues to support our legacy titles, with additional updates coming soon. We encourage anyone aware of additional issues to report them through Activision's Bug Bounty Portal."
How has cheating evolved since you started at Rockstar? We talked about the difference in games, but how have you seen the industry evolve? Has the financial incentive only increased over time, especially as free-to-play games get introduced?
David Andrews: Anytime you're dealing with a free-to-play title, the barrier of entry is just so much lower and that means a broader player population, that means more demand for that title, and more incentive. It’s definitely grown over the years. I think from my particular perspective, the sophistication of the cheat developers is definitely growing as well. [Cheat developers have] their own sort of, we call it OPSEC, operational security, in terms of protecting their identity, because they know what they're doing is not right and they know that the publisher or developer is going to come after them eventually.
So they're getting better and better at hiding themselves from us and working through intermediaries. It’s quite a complex, very interesting sort of threat landscape for us. At the end of the day, it's really evolved over the years. The other thing that's really evolved is cheats used to be pretty simplistic.
They're just hooking, running memory and doing X, Y, Z thing and figuring out what function does what, modifying those functions, and then off to the races. Everybody's anti-cheats have sort of very much pushed them out of the more traditional easy or straightforward ways of cheating. That's why you're seeing growth in other areas like Cronus and other scripted input devices, computer vision powered aim bots, DMA cheats, things that are either reduced in functionality or more expensive, or sometimes both, than what they used to be. The price of a cheat is definitely going up over the years as we all get more and more effective and fight them more consistently.
IGN: Obviously there's software, but there's also hardware like Cronus, physical things that you can purchase. I think Call of Duty has done a pretty good job of trying to stomp that one out, as well as hard platforms in general, like Xbox and PlayStation. How are you guys combating that kind of stuff? It's probably pretty frustrating to know that there's just stuff being sent out in the mail to people. They're just selling it right there. It's not even really hidden.
David Andrews: Cronus and other scripted input devices like that are a really interesting challenge for us. At the end of the day, they do have sort of reduced functionality versus a full blown sheet. So they're usually taking advantage of things like aim assist and just giving it to you all the time or more accurately or whatever.
But absolutely the fact that you can just buy one at a big box store, you can buy one off of any popular online storefront that you might think of, have it shipped to your house and plug it in, and then you're sort of off to the races is definitely frustrating. It also means we've adjusted our enforcement strategy against Cronus as well. It's not the typical enforcement strategy that we have in other places, because we know that for some percentage of these users that are buying a Cronus and plugging it in and getting the advantage off of it, they may not fully realize that that's unauthorized hardware and that it's going to get them banned.
We've actually taken an enforcement stance of, on a first strike, we'll give you a seven-day temporary suspension. We're letting you know you can't use that thing. If you use it again, you're gone forever. And then on a second strike, we catch you using it again, we do permanently suspend that account and there might be implications for your hardware as well, if it's a console or PC or whatever.
We've actually seen pretty good results off of that. We're seeing some rehabilitated behavior. We've certainly gotten some interesting support tickets in that are like, 'I promise I threw away my Cronus. I'll be a good player now. Please let me back in,' that kind of thing, which has been really gratifying to see. The numbers back it up, some percentage of them, which hopefully we can talk about in the future, but some percentage of them are sort of rehabilitating. They take that seven-day suspension and then we don't see any evidence of suspicious gameplay again, which is great. That's where we want to be. For the rest of them, they get permanent bans, they get console or hardware banned, and that's that.
IGN: Is shadow banning a real thing? And what is the argument for why shadow banning works over a permanent ban?
David Andrews: We have limited matchmaking that we will put a suspicious account into to isolate them while other checks are either running or we're waiting on other data. We're kind of doing this review process of looking at that account more holistically and seeing what's really going on here. It's kind of this stopgap measure to immediately remove them without making it be permanent [or without creating] irrevocable impact to that account and to that player, giving us some breathing room to figure out what is going on with this account and then either restoring them to the player population because it was kind of a false alarm situation."
We have also done some rehabilitation through the limited matchmaking saying, 'Hey, you can't do that behavior that you've just been engaged in and you can come back if you stop,' or whatever. We have a lot of enforcement capabilities. We have limited matchmaking, we have ranked play bans, we've got remote play bans, we've got temporary and permanent account suspensions, we've got hardware bans.
We can do all kinds of things, and each time we're dealing with a particular style or type of cheating, we're sort of evaluating which one of these kind of makes sense for this group of cheaters. Can they be rehabilitated? Are we ultimately 100% confident in this? Is more research required? Whatever the case might be, we'll figure out what to do that's appropriate.
IGN: Anything else you want to get off your chest?
David Andrews: Well, recently, we did a bit of a hiring highlight, and back to the point of hiring cheat devs, we collect people from a wide variety of different talent pools. We've got people on the team that are former malware research engineers, theoretical mathematicians. We've got people from the NSA and FBI on the team doing other sorts of work for us. It's a really interesting space to me. Something that doesn't get talked about a lot is the anti-cheat part of the video game industry, because there are no degrees in this stuff. There are no certifications. It's not been commoditized in that way yet, and so you have to reach out and find interesting talent and really bright and passionate people from different parts of different industries altogether and then bring them into games and be like, 'Yeah, now we're going to go chase cheaters around and get them out of Call of Duty now.'
It's an interesting thing. We're always looking for new, interesting talents, no matter what the background is there, constantly growing people ourselves in these roles. It's a really cool part of the industry to be in.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: کودی واکر می‌گوید در صورتی که دختر این بازیگر فقید، میدو واکر موافقت کند، می‌توان از هوش مصنوعی برای بازگرداندن برایان اوکانر پل واکر برای فینال فیلم سریع و خشمگین استفاده کرد.
item.description:
در چت با Entertainment Weekly، کودی واکر گفت که نه او و نه کالب این کار را برای فیلمی که به عنوان آخرین فیلم در مجموعه Fast and Furious تبلیغ می‌شود، انجام نخواهند داد.در عوض، واکر پیشنهاد کرد که می‌توان این بار از هوش مصنوعی برای بازگرداندن برایان استفاده کرد.
کودی گفت: «موضع من این است که میدو [دختر پل] می‌خواهد انجام شود؛ این پدرش است».(Meadow Walker در Fast X نقش آفرینی کرد و وین دیزل حتی او را در راهروی عروسی خود به راه انداخت.)
"من علاقه ای به این کار دوباره ندارم. من عاشق نحوه خروج شخصیت او از فرنچایز هستم. آنها او را نکشتند، آنها چنین کاری را انجام ندادند. این زیبا است، [برایان] بچه هایش را می خواهند."اگر میدو مایلند این را ببینند، در سال 2014 به من نیازی نداشتند یا کالیب چیزی نبود، بنابراین می‌توانستند این کار را انجام دهند.این فرنچایز به سادگی شخصیت برایان اوکانر را بازنشسته می کند.اما همانطور که طرفداران فرنچایز می‌دانند، این دقیقاً همان چیزی نیست که در نهایت اتفاق افتاد.
جاستین لین کارگردان Fast 9 تأیید کرد که برایان اوکانر هنوز در دنیای سریع زنده است.در پایان Furious 7، برایان و دوست دخترش میا تورتو (جوردانا بروستر) از زندگی قانون شکن فرار می کنند تا فرزندان خود را در امنیت بزرگ کنند.و در حالی که شبح واکر در فیلم‌های بعدی سریع و خشمگین وجود دارد، و برایان و میا ذکر شده است، سریال از بازگرداندن مستقیم برایان... تا آخرین صحنه Fast 9 اجتناب کرد.
در Fast 9، میا دوباره به برادر بزرگ‌تر Dom (دیزل) و خدمه می‌پیوندد تا برادرشان را ردیابی کنند (Jakonabde)، جکوناب.میا به دام می گوید که برایان در حالی که در این ماموریت است از همنام خود، پسر نوپای دام برایان، و بچه های خود مراقبت می کند.در پایان، خدمه برای یک شام خانوادگی در خانه Dom در لس آنجلس گرد هم می آیند.یک صندلی خالی است که میا به دام می گوید که سرنشینش در راه است اما دیر می دود.این زمانی است که صحنه به یک ماشین آبی آشنا ختم می‌شود، نیسان اسکای لاین که برایان در فیلم‌های گذشته رانندگی می‌کرد، قبل از اینکه به رنگ سیاه در بیاید، به داخل راه می‌رود.در حالی که ما هرگز راننده را نمی‌بینیم، مفهوم آن واضح است: برایان اوکانر با خانواده‌اش بازگشته است.
دیزل روشن کرده است که احساس می‌کند برای داستان و طرفداران مهم است که برایان اوکانر را برای آخرین بار برای پایان حماسه بازگردانند، که به گفته او شاهد بازگشت این فرنچایز به ریشه‌های مسابقات خیابانی خود خواهیم بود.دیزل در سال 2023 به توتال فیلم گفت: «نمی‌توانستم تصور کنم این حماسه بدون خداحافظی واقعی با برایان اوکانر به پایان برسد.
در ژانویه، دیزل تاریخ اکران و عنوان دنباله Fast X را در یک پست اینستاگرامی با استفاده از عکسی از شخصیت‌های او و واکر در فیلم اصلی 2001 اعلام کرد: «هیچ‌کس نمی‌گفت که مسیر ما آسان است.میراث... و یک میراث... برای همیشه لطفا برای همیشه سریع باشید."
Fast Forever توسط لوئیس لتریر کارگردانی می شود که فیلم Fast X را نیز کارگردانی کرد، که با نقدهای ضعیفی روبرو شد و ثابت شد که کم درآمدترین فیلم در این مجموعه است.ژیزل یاشار در فیلم‌های کوتاهی که به وضوح آنها را به عنوان بازگشت برای فیلم بعدی و پایانی تعیین می‌کند.زمان نشان خواهد داد که آیا واقعاً این اتفاق می افتد یا خیر.

item.title: صداپیشه افسانه ای مایک مک فارلند در سن 56 سالگی درگذشت و میراثی غیرقابل انکار با صدها نقش در برخی از نمادین ترین سریال های انیمیشنی که تا کنون ساخته شده است، از خود به جای گذاشت.
item.description:
Ageland Die Legend.میراثی غیرقابل انکار با صدها نقش در برخی از نمادین‌ترین مجموعه‌های انیمیشنی که تا به حال ساخته شده است، پشت سر گذاشت.
خبر مرگ مک فارلند در ساعات پایانی ۹ سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶ منتشر شد. این بازیگر بیشتر به خاطر صداپیشگی استاد روشی از Dragon Ball، ژان کرستاین در Attack on the Titanean, Buggly، در فیلم Attack on the Titanean, Buggly، معروف بود.کیمیاگر، و بسیاری از شخصیت‌های دیگر.
اگر از طرفداران انیمیشن هستید، احتمالاً نام مک فارلین را شنیده‌اید.فعالیت حرفه ای او در اواخر دهه 90 با سریال توپ اژدها شروع شد و بعداً به نمایش های برجسته دیگری مانند یویو هاکوشو (کومادا، بوتاجیری) و سبد میوه (ریسو سوما) پرداخت.
در آگوست 2025، تشخیص داده شد که مک فارلند به گلیوبلاستوما، نوعی سرطان تهاجمی مغز، مبتلا شده است.صداپیشگان همکار او برای ایجاد GoFundMe برای کمک به جمع‌آوری پول برای هزینه‌های پزشکی او گرد هم آمدند، با افرادی مانند جی مایکل تیتوم (سباستین مایکلیس، اروین اسمیت) که در مورد این موضوع در Twitter/X پست گذاشت.
تعدادی از صداپیشه‌های مطرح، کهنه‌کارها و طرفداران این صنعت پس از مرگ او صحبت کردند.
بیست سال، روح کمیاب‌تر و زیباتر این دنیا هرگز نمی‌شناسد، عشقی که تو آفریده‌ای، دوام می‌آورد، اما لعنتی اگر بدانم بدون تو چطور پیش می‌رویم.
مایک مک‌فارلند، دوست عزیزم، بیش از بیست سال است.روح نادرتر و زیباتر این دنیا هرگز نخواهد شناخت.آرام باش نمکعشقی که تو آفریدی پابرجاست، اما لعنتی اگر بدانم بدون تو چطور پیش می‌رویم و آن را با او به اشتراک می‌گذاریم.💔 pic.twitter.com/aUr99fsqjX
الخاندرو ساب، صدای ددپول در Marvel Rivals نیز صحبت کرد.او نوشت: "او احمق، مهربان و باهوش بود... همیشه توصیه های غذایی عالی داشت. خواننده عالی! یک بازیگر و کارگردان باورنکردنی، اما شما بچه ها این را می دانید، و اگر فکر می کنید اینطور نیست، به من اعتماد کنید، دارید.""این واقعاً به نظر واقعی نمی رسد؟ مثل اینکه هنوز به این نتیجه نرسیده است که درست است و این مایه شرمساری است... اما من همیشه می خواستم بیشتر شبیه مایک باشم. بیشتر سفر کنید و در واقع از جایی که می بینم لذت ببرید. به کنسرت های بیشتری بروید! حتی وقتی موسیقی را نمی دانم. غذاهایی را که امتحان نکرده بودم امتحان کنید."او را می‌شناخت، و برای همه طرفداران انیمه که کار او را می‌شناختند، او یک استعداد باورنکردنی بود، یک دوست خوب برای بسیاری از ما، و به شدت دلتنگ خواهد شد."او احمق، مهربان و باهوش بود... همیشه توصیه های غذایی عالی داشت.خواننده بزرگ!یک بازیگر و کارگردان باورنکردنی، اما شما بچه ها این را می دانید، و اگر فکر می کنید این کار را نمی کنید، به من اعتماد کنید، می دانید.این فقط احساس نمی‌کند...
هنوز دیگران لحظات دل‌انگیز سال‌ها پیش را به یاد می‌آورند، با یکی از طرفداران که پس از به اشتراک گذاشتن کلیپی از بازیگری که بازیگران خود را در کلوپ میزبان دبیرستان اوران فاش می‌کرد، در فضای مجازی پخش شد، جایی که او با لباس شخصیت خود به صحنه رفت.
به یاد مایک مک‌فارلند، اجازه دهید زمانی را به یاد بیاوریم که @caitlinst او را در اعلامیه‌ی School Host Host Voice معرفی کرد.2008 و او کاملاً با لباس رانکا ظاهر شد.انسان واقعاً فداکار بود. منبع: https://t.co/ta906PihjX pic.twitter.com/PPjYdiW8Nv
می‌دانم که او بیشتر برای نقش‌های دیگر شناخته شده بود، اما همیشه برای من نش خواهد بود... شنیدن این موضوع بسیار ناراحت کننده است... من شخصاً با او ملاقات کردم و او به من گفت که هیچ صدای ضبط شده‌ای را به صورت رایگان از من انجام نمی‌دهد، اما وقتی او همه چیزهای ضبط شده من را به صورت رایگان انجام نمی‌دهد.مک فارلند با بازی های درخشان و به یاد ماندنی خود در طول زندگی حرفه ای خود زندگی بسیاری از طرفداران را تحت تأثیر قرار داد. دهه ها کار او به عنوان صداپیشه، فیلمنامه نویس، کارگردان ADR، تهیه کننده و بسیاری از صداپیشگان در صنعت انگلیسی در طول زندگی خود شکل داد.ما می دانیم که Words نمی تواند تأثیر او را به طور کامل در جهان تعریف کند، اما امروز به یاد مایک مک فارلند انیمه تماشا کنید@TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: بازی دزدی آنلاین پلی‌استیشن، Fairgames، ظاهراً با نام رمز با اولین گیم‌پلی دوباره ظاهر شد و به یک تست بازی دعوت می‌کند.
item.description:
بازی دزدی آنلاین پلی‌استیشن، Fairgames، ظاهراً با اولین گیم‌پلی با نام رمز دوباره ظاهر شده و به یک تست پلی استیشن دعوت می‌شود.
سه سال پیش، پلی‌استیشن یک شوتر آنلاین جدید به نام Fairgames را معرفی کرد.این یک بازی دزدی رقابتی است که بر روی کاغذ یک مفهوم نسبتاً منحصر به فرد است، اما طبق گزارش ها انواع مشکلات توسعه، از جمله جدایی بنیانگذار استودیو Jade Raymond و مدیر خلاق بازی، Daniel Drapeau را داشته است.خروج آنها پس از آن اتفاق افتاد که کارکنان داخل استودیو به دنبال تست های منفی داخلی بازی شروع به ابراز نگرانی در مورد بازی کردند.این بازی از زمان معرفی تا حد زیادی توسط پلی استیشن تایید نشده است، اما توسعه آن ادامه یافته است.
اکنون، ظاهراً این بازی کاملاً با نام رمز Project Espresso دوباره ظاهر شده است.این بازی به Player.gg اضافه شد، وب‌سایتی که به توسعه‌دهندگان اجازه می‌دهد با بازیکنان برای تست بازی ارتباط برقرار کنند.اگرچه این بازی تحت نام رمز قرار دارد و توسعه‌دهنده آن مخفی نگه داشته شده است، این لیست شامل یک تریلر گیم‌پلی بسیار قابل توجهی است که به‌طور چشمگیری شبیه به Fairgames است.این یک سبک هنری و مفهوم مشابه دارد و یک سلب مسئولیت وجود دارد که بازی برای PS5 و PC در حال توسعه است.
به نظر می‌رسد این اولین نگاه رسمی به گیم‌پلی برای FAIRGAME$ با نام مستعار Break In است https://t.co/kuphMNor1Y pic.twitter.com/W5KE8nEO9b
این بازی باید به طور کامل انجام شود.معمولا برای یک بازی شخص ثالث اتفاق می افتد.همه چیز کمی عجیب است، اما تصور اینکه چیز دیگری باشد سخت است.و اگر می‌خواهید خودتان آن را بررسی کنید، می‌توانید برای یک تست پخش در Player.gg ثبت‌نام کنید.
اوایل امسال، PlayStation همچنین یک علامت تجاری برای یک بازی جدید به نام Break In ثبت کرد، که برخی گمان می‌برند عنوان جدید Fairgames باشد.IGN برای اظهار نظر در مورد وضعیت به پلی استیشن مراجعه کرده است و اگر چیزی بشنویم داستان را به‌روزرسانی می‌کند.
اگرچه Fairgames تا حد زیادی مخفی شده است، اما این موضوع مانع از شک و تردید گیمرها نشده است.دیگر سرویس زنده بزرگ پلی استیشن، کنکورد، یک بمب فاجعه بار بود.علاوه بر این، Marathon نتوانسته است تحت تأثیر قرار بگیرد، The Last of Us Online لغو شد، Destiny 2 دیگر پشتیبانی نمی‌شود، و اخیراً یک نفرت عمومی نسبت به بازی‌های سرویس زنده وجود دارد.در خارج از عرضه‌های شخص اول پلی‌استیشن، Highguard قرار بود یکی دیگر از عنوان‌های سرویس زنده بزرگ دیگر باشد، اما در عرض دو ماه از بین رفت.
این که آیا Fairgames (یا هر نام نهایی آن در پایان می‌آید) می‌تواند روندها را کاهش دهد و مردم را علاقه‌مند کند، باید دید.زمان جالبی برای سونی است زیرا بی وقفه در حال پیمایش در هرج و مرج است.دیشب، پس از برنامه ریزی پلتفرم برای لغو بازی جاه طلبانه نسل بعدی کوجیما، Physint، تایید شد که Hideo Kojima از پلی استیشن جدا می شود.ایکس باکس وارد عمل شد و پیشنهاد نجات آن را داد و رابطه شرکت با مؤلف را تقویت کرد.کوجیما همچنین در حال توسعه یک بازی ترسناک جدید با ایکس باکس است که با نام OD شناخته می‌شود.
پلی‌استیشن پس از تصمیم‌های خود مبنی بر قطع پشتیبانی از رسانه‌های فیزیکی در سال 2028، خاموش کردن Bluepoint چند سال پس از خرید آن و پایان دادن به پشتیبانی از بازی‌های تک‌نفره روی رایانه شخصی، با بازیکنان روبرو شده است.یکی دیگر از بمب‌های سرویس زنده در حال حاضر ضربه بزرگی به روابط عمومی پلی‌استیشن خواهد بود، بنابراین امیدواریم این تست‌های پخش بتواند آن را به چیزی جذاب برای مخاطبان گسترده تبدیل کند.
کید اوندر یک فریلنسر برای تیم خبری IGN است.او همه چیزهای سرگرمی، از جمله بازی، فیلم و موارد دیگر را پوشش می دهد.می توانید او را در توییتر @Cade_Onder پیدا کنید.

item.title: فیلم مردان ایکس مارول فرشته خود را در آسا ژرمن پیدا کرده است که بیشتر به خاطر نقش‌هایش در Gen V و Scream 7 شناخته می‌شود.
item.description:
طبق گزارش هالیوود ریپورتر، Germann در واقع برای قسمت Cyclops تست داده بود که در نهایت به کیت کانر رسید.با این حال، او از رقابت خارج نشد و اکنون در نقش وارن ورتینگتون III (که بیشتر با نام مستعار خود فرشته شناخته می شود) ایکس من را بازی می کند.
در 28 سالگی، ژرمن در کنار سادی سینک 24 ساله (23-آند گری) (Jean Boy-year) به جمع بازیگرانی می پیوندد که جوان تر هستند.ایند ناوارت 25 ساله، که ماه گذشته در کنفرانس هواداران دیزنی D23 تایید شد که نقش Rogue را بازی می کند.
از دیگر بازیگران تایید شده می توان به سامارا ویوینگ در نقش اما فراست و کریستوفر ابوت در نقش چارلز خاویر اشاره کرد، و آدام درایور قرار است نقش شخصیت شرور را بازی کند، اگرچه German Cyclops's، این را نگفت.استودیو به قدری تحت تاثیر تست بازیگری او قرار گرفت که تصمیم گرفتند او را به عنوان فرشته انتخاب کنند.این قلمرو کاملاً جدید برای بازیگر نیست.او با جهان‌های ابرقهرمانی کاملاً آشنا است، او در سریال «پسرها» Gen V نقش سم ریوردان را بازی کرده است، شخصیتی با قدرت مافوق بشری، استقامت، تحرک، و شنوایی، از جمله ویژگی‌های دیگر.
با توجه به بال‌هایش و همه این‌ها، ابرقدرت‌های فرشته همگی به پرندگان مربوط می‌شوند.این شخصیت اخیراً یکی از موضوعات محبوب رسانه‌های اجتماعی بوده است، به طوری که طرفداران صحنه‌ای دلخراش را از مردان ایکس در سال 2006 به یاد می‌آورند: آخرین جایگاه که در آن او در کودکی پرهایش را بیرون می‌کشید.
اولین بار که در سال 1963 در کمیک مردان ایکس شماره 1 ظاهر شد، یکی از اعضای بنیان‌گذار مردان ایکس به‌عنوان ثروتمندترین ما و او بود.او قبل از پیوستن به گروه به عنوان یک مراقب تحت نام فرشته انتقام‌جویانه فعالیت می‌کرد و در نهایت با دست آخرالزمان به فرشته‌ای در حال فکر با بال‌های فلزی تبدیل شد.
بازیگران مردان ایکس مارول با گذشت ماه‌ها همچنان به نمایش در می‌آیند، چیزی که رئیس استودیوی مارول، کوین فایگی، گفته بود در D2 رخ خواهد داد.از نظر ظاهری، این بازیگران اینجاست که می‌ماند، زیرا فایگه داستان‌هایی درباره مردان ایکس که هنوز گفته نشده‌اند، «حماسه‌ها بر حماسه‌ها» را طعنه می‌زند.
فایگی گفت: «با داشتن 85، تقریبا 90 سال تاریخ کمیک، هنوز داستان‌های زیادی برای گفتن وجود دارد.او در پنل Disney Worldbuilers در D23 گفت: "روز گذشته یک بازیگر بسیار جوان و جدید را برای ملکی به نام X-Men معرفی کردیم. و این عالی است، زیرا 10 فیلم عالی X-Men وجود دارد [اما] می تواند 100 فیلم دیگر نیز وجود داشته باشد."
ویرجینیا (او) سردبیر اخبار IGN است.او با ده سال تجربه گزارش در مورد بازی‌ها و سرگرمی‌ها، سابقه‌ای در جامعه بازی‌های مبارزه‌ای، اخبار اینفلوئنسرها و روندهای آنلاین ویروسی دارد.او را در توییتر در @TheeMissGlaze بیابید.
